title: a match unique only within a cut answer is not accepted
line: the geocoder is asked for six candidates and its answer for Bandon, Ireland holds six, the town and five stretches of the river: a full page may be cut, so the one place verified on it is not accepted until the query is asked again for the most one request gives, and a geocoder that cannot be asked that leaves the string as it was, kept for the next run, no card and no place

steps.say: the birthplace a FamilySearch results row writes for Jams Aherne or Aherre, born 19 January 1906, as the owner's catalog holds it
the resolver run with the geocoder's real six-candidate answer and Wikidata's item for the town planted, the geocoder silent beyond its cache

expect.why: the town is the one place on the page that verifies, but the page holds as many candidates as were asked for: nothing is accepted on it, and the wider request found no geocoder, so the string is left as it was
a string the geocoder did not answer gets no card: the next run asks again

has: 1 string(s) left as they were; run again

expect.why: the run says it left the string because the geocoder did not answer the wider request; the first page's answer in the cache is never served for it
